    <dependency>

    <dependency>

    </dependency>

1	# OfficeFloor REST wiring
2	
3	Domain REST endpoints are declared here as **additive OfficeFloor YAML**, served by the
4	officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter inside the Spring Boot host. Put them under `rest/api/` so
5	their paths start with `/api/` — `SpaConfig` only bypasses the SPA deep-link fallback for `/api/*`
6	(a non-`/api/` route returns the SPA HTML instead of your endpoint). Directory nesting maps to path
7	segments, so `rest/api/owners.GET.yml` → `GET /api/owners`. Each route is its own file:
8	
9	```
10	# officefloor/rest/api/<path>.GET.yml   (or .POST.yml, {param}.GET.yml, ...)
11	service:
12	  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.<SomeLogic>   # a class with a service(...) method
13	```
14	
15	The logic class's `service(...)` method takes injected dependencies (Spring @Service beans, the
16	data layer) and a `net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse<T>` to send the response — verified shape:
17	OfficeFloor tutorial SpringRestGettingStartedHttpServer.
18	
19	This directory is a **shared surface** (`config.yaml → app.shared_surfaces.backend`): the additive
20	ideal is a **new .yml + a new logic class per endpoint**, never growing a central file — a
21	checkpoint forced to edit shared wiring scores a boundary violation (DESIGN.md §8).
22	
23	The base has no domain routes; cp01 onward add them. (The `/__test__` seed endpoint and readiness
24	`/actuator/health` are Spring-side — a @RestController and Actuator — not OfficeFloor routes.)
25

# OfficeFloor REST wiring

Domain REST endpoints are declared here as **additive OfficeFloor YAML**, served by the
officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter inside the Spring Boot host. Put them under `rest/api/` so
their paths start with `/api/` — `SpaConfig` only bypasses the SPA deep-link fallback for `/api/*`
(a non-`/api/` route returns the SPA HTML instead of your endpoint). Directory nesting maps to path
segments, so `rest/api/owners.GET.yml` → `GET /api/owners`. Each route is its own file:

```
# officefloor/rest/api/<path>.GET.yml   (or .POST.yml, {param}.GET.yml, ...)
service:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.<SomeLogic>   # a class with a service(...) method
```

The logic class's `service(...)` method takes injected dependencies (Spring @Service beans, the
data layer) and a `net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse<T>` to send the response — verified shape:
OfficeFloor tutorial SpringRestGettingStartedHttpServer.

This directory is a **shared surface** (`config.yaml → app.shared_surfaces.backend`): the additive
ideal is a **new .yml + a new logic class per endpoint**, never growing a central file — a
checkpoint forced to edit shared wiring scores a boundary violation (DESIGN.md §8).

The base has no domain routes; cp01 onward add them. (The `/__test__` seed endpoint and readiness
`/actuator/health` are Spring-side — a @RestController and Actuator — not OfficeFloor routes.)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The agent's test loop (DESIGN.md §15): build, start the whole app, run ONLY the specs currently
# present in e2e/specs (the agent sees only its own checkpoint's spec — blind), then stop.
# PINNED — do not edit. Contract: BASE_CHECKLIST.md §C, §D.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# Wait for readiness (Actuator health), then run the Playwright specs against BASE_URL.
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done

# Install deps + the Chromium browser (both cached after first run), then run the specs.

All 3 tests pass. The change is implemented as a full-stack, additive change:

**What I did** — enforced that every client must have a proper email address, across all three layers:

- **Database** (`V2__client_email_format.sql`): new Flyway migration adding a `CHECK` constraint (`REGEXP_LIKE`) so a blank/malformed email can never be persisted.
- **Server** (`CreateClientLogic.java`): validates the submitted email against an email regex and throws `HttpException(BAD_REQUEST)` without saving if it's missing or malformed.
- **Front-end** (`ClientsPage.tsx`): validates on submit, surfaces a `client-form-email-error` element and blocks the POST when the email is invalid (also handles a server rejection), so no client row is created.

All three layers share the same email shape (`^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$`). The existing `data-testid` anchors are untouched; the only new one is `client-form-email-error`, which the spec requires. Tests: 3 passed (blank rejected, malformed rejected, valid accepted).
